claims.text: Increasing configurational entropy at the RE site creates a more homogeneous local lattice environment.
A more homogeneous local lattice environment minimizes spatial fluctuations in pairing-related interactions such as spin fluctuations or Josephson coupling.
The baseline consists of polycrystalline, single-RE REBa2Cu3O7–δ in the oxygenated orthorhombic phase.
The orthorhombic REBa2Cu3O7–δ phase has space group Pmmm.
Mixing four or five RE elements at the RE site increases configurational entropy relative to a single-RE baseline.
Single-RE and mixed-RE samples should be compared using identical oxygen partial pressure and heat-treatment profiles.
Controlling oxygen stoichiometry and microstructure isolates the effect of RE-site configurational entropy.
High RE-site configurational entropy reduces strain variations in the CuO2 planes and improves lattice uniformity.
XRD peak broadening, lattice-parameter consistency, and TEM strain mapping can quantify the proposed lattice-uniformity mediator.
A more uniform lattice reduces spatial fluctuations in magnetic exchange interactions.
A more uniform lattice reduces variations in inter-grain Josephson coupling.
Reduced interaction fluctuations minimize superconducting phase inhomogeneity and strengthen superconducting coherence.
Electron–phonon coupling modifications are less central than magnetic or Josephson-coupling effects in cuprate superconductivity.
High-entropy samples will have a narrower superconducting transition than the single-RE baseline.
High-entropy samples will have a modestly higher Tc than the single-RE baseline.
High-entropy samples will have enhanced intra-grain critical current density relative to low-entropy or single-RE samples.
The enhancement of intra-grain critical current density is most evident at 2.0–4.2 K and is not clearly observed at 20 K.
Pairing interactions are most sensitive to local lattice uniformity at approximately 2–4 K.
Failure to maintain oxygen stoichiometry can diminish or obscure the configurational-entropy effect.
Spin-fluctuation, inter-grain Josephson-coupling, and flux-pinning contributions cannot be distinguished by the proposed measurements alone.

contradictions.description: The stated 2–20 K measurement range cannot determine Tc or transition width for RE123, whose Tc is reported by the cited evidence to exceed 90 K.
